title: Chat and citations won't save your vertical AI - Atul Ramachandran, Filed Inc
talk_summary: A CTO of a vertical tax-AI company argues that chat and citations alone fail because chat is synchronous and citations push verification back onto users; instead products should be built as a 'conveyor belt' where users delegate long-running tasks to background agents and act as supervisors. He lays out four components: delegatable long tasks, skills to capture user-specific conventions, monitoring/traces, and control (pause/intervene, plan approval for irreversible actions), plus a metric shift from weekly active users to weekly active sessions.

takeaways.technique: Target long-running repeatable tasks as the unit of delegation
takeaways.what_they_do: They identify tasks in the user workflow that take more than an hour and are repeatable, and build long-running background agents around those rather than around interactive chat turns.
takeaways.evidence_quote: find tasks that your users do that take more than a couple of hours ... these tasks are what you use to build what you call a long-running background agents

takeaways.technique: Capture per-repo conventions as skills, ideally auto-derived from usage
takeaways.what_they_do: They treat the last 20% (quirks, conventions, house style) as the real value and capture it as skills, auto-generating them from product usage rather than asking users to author skills in a separate UI.
When the agent is about to make an assumption, the run pauses and a supervisor replies in a chat-like thread to resolve the conflict, then the belt restarts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: pausing whenever the agent was trying to make an assumption, we pause. And then the users would come in just like in Slack

takeaways.what_they_do: Before dangerous/irreversible steps (e.g., data entry that can erase existing data) they present a plan for approval rather than executing directly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: some actions are usually irreversible and are dangerous actions. And in those cases, you need to present a plan

takeaways.what_they_do: They trace every value the agent produced in a user-readable format and keep a task list showing processing state per task, because long runs have many moving pieces.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we trace back each and every value that the AI agent produced ... This is where the trust is built

takeaways.technique: Measure completed sessions, not active users
takeaways.what_they_do: They shift the success metric from weekly active users to weekly active sessions, i.e., tasks completed by an agent even when the human is absent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: weekly active sessions ... a task that is completed by a human or an agent even when the user is not in your platform
